couplets.gloss: A dream has brought me word from the one I love: how can I possibly thank it enough?

edges.reason: The dream arrives like a guest bearing his message, and she wonders how to honour it.
edges.quote: the dream that came with a message from my lover

couplets.gloss: If only I could get my eyes to sleep, I could go to him in a dream and tell him how I'm still somehow surviving.

edges.reason: Sleep is the only road left to him, and it is shut until she can fall asleep.
edges.quote: I could tell the one who held me

edges.reason: Treats her wakeful eyes as someone she has to talk round before she can reach him.
edges.quote: would sleep when I beg them

couplets.gloss: He won't come near me when I'm awake, so seeing him while I sleep is the one thing that keeps me going.

edges.reason: Seeing him in dreams is all that holds her to life while he stays away.
edges.quote: I see him in dreams, and that is what keeps me alive

couplets.sensitive: Ties staying alive to an absent lover.

couplets.gloss: Dreaming gives me the love I'm missing, because it finds him and brings him back when, awake, he shows me no pity.

edges.reason: The dream does what he will not: it seeks him out, brings him to her and gives her the joy of desire.
edges.quote: a dream seeks out the man

couplets.gloss: A dream is only sweet while it lasts, but then so was seeing him in real life: both are over the moment they end.

edges.reason: Puts dream and waking on one level, since each is sweet only while he is in view.
edges.quote: The dream too is sweet only while I am seeing it

couplets.gloss: If only there were no such thing as being awake: the dream wouldn't stop and he would never leave me.
couplets.sensitive: wishes never to wake, as an escape from pain

edges.reason: Waking is cast as the enemy that breaks off the dream and takes him from her again.
edges.quote: If there were no such thing as waking

couplets.gloss: He's heartless enough to ignore me when I'm awake, so why does he come and torment me when I'm asleep?
keywords: can't stop dreaming about my ex

edges.reason: Here the comfort sours: the man who shows no kindness when she is awake won’t leave her alone in her dreams.
edges.quote: Why does he torment me in my dreams?

couplets.gloss: While I sleep he is in my arms, and the second I wake he rushes straight back into my heart.
keywords: thinking of him all the time

edges.reason: Asleep he holds her, as in a dream; awake he darts into her heart, so she is never without him.
edges.quote: When I sleep, he is on my shoulders.

couplets.gloss: People blame him for never turning up, but that's only because they don't get to see him in their dreams as I do.

edges.reason: Answers those who fault his absence: they have not met him in sleep as she has.
edges.quote: never see a lover in their dreams

couplets.gloss: The neighbours say he has left me. Can it be that they just don't see him in their sleep the way I do?

edges.reason: Her retort to the talk: how can he have gone, when she meets him in sleep?
edges.quote: not see him in their dreams

edges.reason: Turns on the neighbours who announce he has gone, and asks what they can know of it.
edges.quote: They say he left me in waking life

couplets.gloss: You're no mere evening: you are the time of day that eats away the life of anyone whose partner has gone.

edges.reason: Refuses the hour its gentle name and calls it a devourer of lives.
edges.quote: the time that eats the lives

couplets.gloss: Evening, you look as sad and washed out as I feel: is your partner as hard-hearted as mine?

edges.reason: Sees her own sorrow in the dusk and asks it whether it too has a hard-hearted mate.
edges.quote: Is your mate as hard-hearted as mine?

couplets.gloss: Evening used to arrive shy and gentle; now it walks right up to me and brings nothing but misery.

edges.reason: Evening buds with cold and turns pale, and as it comes her own despair buds and her pain grows.
edges.quote: despair buds in me and pain grows

couplets.gloss: When the one you love is away, evening comes towards you like the man sent to carry out a death sentence.

edges.reason: Dusk comes to the woman left alone as strangers come to a killing ground.
edges.quote: evening comes like strangers to a killing ground

couplets.gloss: What did I ever do for the morning that it treats me so kindly, and what did I do to the evening that it hurts me so?

edges.reason: Puzzles over the two hours as if they were people, one she had helped and one she had wronged.
edges.quote: what harm did I do the evening?

couplets.gloss: As long as my love was beside me, I had no idea how much an evening could hurt.

edges.reason: Evening brought no pain until he left: its cruelty is the work of his absence.
edges.quote: I never knew that evening brings pain

couplets.gloss: This love-sickness starts small at dawn, grows all through the day, and is at its very worst by evening.

edges.reason: Charts the whole course of her grief in one day, from first stirring at dawn to its height at dusk.
edges.quote: buds in the morning, fills out all day and flowers in the evening

edges.reason: Pain opens as a flower opens, petal by petal through the daylight hours.
edges.quote: goeth on opening its petals the livelong day

edges.reason: Evening is the hour at which the bloom of suffering stands fully open.
edges.quote: flowers in the evening

edges.reason: Names what she feels as an illness, with its own regular daily course.
edges.quote: This sickness

couplets.gloss: They call it a shepherd's flute, but to me it's a deadly weapon, because its sound announces the evening that burns me.

edges.reason: Even a cowherd’s flute is dreaded, because it is the messenger of this hour.
edges.quote: The cowherd’s flute is a messenger for the evening

edges.reason: Dusk scorches her, a fire that comes in on the sound of a flute.
edges.quote: the evening that burns like fire

couplets.gloss: If this evening that has already unhinged me comes on any further, I will die and the whole town will be left in mourning.
couplets.sensitive: speaks of dying of grief and the town mourning

edges.reason: As evening spreads it takes reason with it, until the town itself reels and suffers.
edges.quote: When evening spreads and reason reels

couplets.gloss: My life has hung on so far but it will give out now, as evening makes me think of the man who cares only about money.
couplets.sensitive: speaks of life ebbing away from grief

edges.reason: Evening wounds here through memory, calling up the man whose way is wealth.
edges.quote: as I think of the man whose way is wealth

couplets.gloss: Thinking of the man who claimed he was leaving for my happiness, my faded eyes can't face the flowers for shame.

edges.reason: Her eyes feel shame as a person would, now that thinking of him has dimmed them.
edges.quote: your eyes now shrink in shame

edges.reason: Flowers are the standard of beauty that her faded eyes can no longer stand beside.
edges.quote: before sweet flowers

couplets.gloss: My dull, streaming eyes seem to be telling everyone how unkind he has been to me.
keywords: can't hide that i've been crying

edges.reason: Her tears run and tell others what she would rather keep to herself.
edges.quote: streaming with tears

edges.reason: Turned informer, her eyes give away the very man they love.
edges.quote: seem to be telling of the unkindness

couplets.gloss: These arms that filled out with happiness on my wedding day now seem to be announcing to everyone that he has gone.
My arms lost their old beauty when he left, and now they've grown so thin that my bangles drop off on their own.

edges.reason: Her arms have thinned since he left, until the gold bangles slip away.
edges.quote: the gold bangles slip away

couplets.gloss: My arms, robbed of their beauty and their bangles, tell the whole world how cruel he has been.

edges.reason: Bare arms and lost bangles together become a public charge against him.
edges.quote: their bangles gone and their old beauty withered, tell of the cruelty

couplets.gloss: I scold my arms for getting thin and losing my bangles, because now people are calling him cruel.

edges.reason: Her thin arms and slipping bangles draw the charge that he is cruel, and that charge is what hurts her.
edges.quote: my bangles slip

couplets.gloss: Heart, if you want to earn some credit, go to that cruel man and tell him of the talk my thinning arm has started.
keywords: want him to know how i feel

edges.reason: Dispatches her heart as a messenger to him, and offers it glory for the errand.
edges.quote: Will you win glory, my heart

couplets.gloss: We were holding each other once and I let my arms go a little slack, and at once her forehead lost its colour.

edges.reason: A moment’s slackening of his arms is parting enough to drain her forehead.
edges.quote: the forehead of that simple girl in gold bangles turned pale

couplets.gloss: Just one breath of air slipped between us as we held each other, and the colour left her big eyes straight away.

edges.reason: A thin draught through their embrace is enough to blanch her eyes.
edges.quote: a cool breeze cut through our embrace

couplets.gloss: Her eyes didn't only lose their colour: they cried as well, seeing what had happened to her forehead.

edges.reason: Pallor is treated as a person: the pallor in her eyes suffers at what her forehead has done.
edges.quote: the pallor in her eyes suffered

edges.reason: Her eyes look on like a person, distressed at what her forehead has done.
edges.quote: when it saw what her bright forehead had done

couplets.gloss: Heart, can't you think of something, anything at all, that would cure me of this sickness nothing seems to cure?

edges.reason: Begs her heart to work out what she herself cannot.
edges.quote: Won’t you think of something, heart

edges.reason: Her suffering is a sickness that won’t end, and she goes looking for a cure anyway.
edges.quote: this unending sickness

couplets.gloss: Good luck to you, heart, but it's stupid to go on suffering over someone who has no love for you.

edges.reason: Calls it plain folly to keep grieving for a man who has no love to give.
edges.quote: That is foolishness

edges.reason: Scolds the heart to its face, closing on a mocking blessing.
edges.quote: my heart, long may you live

edges.reason: Says to the grieving self what a blunt friend would: he does not love you, so stop suffering for him.
edges.quote: He has no love for you, yet you go on suffering

couplets.gloss: Heart, what's the point of sitting here wasting away over him? The man who did this to us isn't thinking of us at all.

edges.reason: Asks what good it does to sit aching for a man who has no tender thought for her.
edges.quote: Why sit here thinking of him and aching

edges.reason: Speaks to the heart as a partner in a useless vigil she now wants to end.
edges.quote: Why sit here thinking of him and aching, heart?

edges.reason: A plain argument for anyone stuck: the one who gave you this sickness has no tender thought for you.
edges.quote: has no tender thought for us

couplets.gloss: Heart, if you're going to him, take my eyes along too, because they're eating me alive with wanting to see him.
keywords: can't stop wanting to see him

edges.reason: Sends the heart off to him and hands it the eyes as extra baggage.
edges.quote: Take my eyes with you too when you go, heart

edges.reason: Starved of the sight of him, the eyes gnaw at her like tormentors.
edges.quote: Wanting to see him, they are eating me

couplets.gloss: He pushes me away however hard I hold on, yet can I really write him off as an enemy, heart?
keywords: still loyal to someone who rejected me
couplets.sensitive: treats clinging to someone who spurns you as the only course

edges.reason: Puts the hard question to her heart rather than answering it herself.
edges.quote: Can we give him up as an enemy, heart?

couplets.gloss: Heart, you drop your grudge and run to him the moment you see him, so I suspect even this anger of yours is just an act.

edges.reason: Catches her heart bluffing: it scolds him now but will melt at first sight of him.
edges.quote: Your anger now is a pretence, my heart

couplets.gloss: Heart, let go of either the love or the shyness: I can't carry the two of them at once.

edges.reason: Hands her heart an ultimatum, since she herself can no longer hold both.
edges.quote: give up desire or give up modesty

couplets.gloss: You moan that he won't come back out of pity, and you'd chase him even though he left on purpose. Heart, you're an idiot.

edges.reason: By mocking the heart for going after a man who left, she sides with holding back.
edges.quote: you go after the one who left

edges.reason: Ends her quarrel with the heart on a flat insult.
edges.quote: You are a fool, my heart.

edges.reason: Tells anyone tempted to go after someone who left that pining and pursuit are a fool’s way.
edges.quote: you go after the one who left

couplets.gloss: Who exactly are you trying to reach, heart, when the one you love is already living inside you?

edges.reason: Points out to the restless heart that what it runs after is already within it.
edges.quote: Your lover is within you, my heart.

couplets.gloss: As long as we keep holding in our heart the man who walked out on us, we'll go on losing more of ourselves.

edges.reason: Warns that cherishing the man who left will only wear her down further.
edges.quote: we will lose still more of our beauty

edges.reason: States the cost outright: keeping someone who left in your heart costs you more of your beauty.
edges.quote: If we keep in our heart the one who left us

couplets.gloss: However firmly shyness has locked the door of self-possession, strong love will simply break it down.

edges.reason: Desire is the axe no door of reserve withstands, even one bolted with modesty.
edges.quote: The axe of desire breaks down the door

couplets.gloss: Love has no mercy: it keeps its grip on my heart even in the middle of the night.
keywords: can't sleep for thinking of him

edges.reason: Sums up desire in one word, merciless, for the hold it keeps on her heart.
edges.quote: This thing called desire has no mercy.

edges.reason: The dead of night, when all else rests, brings her no relief from it.
edges.quote: even in the dead of night

couplets.gloss: I really do try to keep my love hidden, but it bursts out by itself with no warning, the way a sneeze does.

edges.reason: Desire does not ask leave to show itself, however she tries to keep it in.
edges.quote: it comes out without warning

edges.reason: A sneeze measures how little the will has to do with desire coming out.
edges.quote: like a sneeze

couplets.gloss: I used to pride myself on my composure, but love has torn through all that and put itself on public display.
keywords: everyone can see i'm in love

couplets.gloss: The proud self-respect that won't go after someone who hurt you is simply unknown to people sick with love.
couplets.sensitive: treats running after one who hurt you as natural

edges.reason: Names the dignity that won’t go after those who hurt you, then says the sickness of desire has none of it.
edges.quote: The great dignity of not going after those who hurt you

couplets.gloss: Thanks a lot, sorrow! You care for me so much that you want me to run after the man who cruelly left me.
The moment the one I love shows me affection, I forget I ever had any shyness.
It's the soft-spoken pleading of that charming liar that breaks down all my womanly defences.
I set out meaning to sulk and stay away, but I ended up holding him, because I could see my heart had already gone over.
People whose hearts melt like fat on a flame can't possibly claim they will hold out and refuse to make up.

edges.reason: A heart yields as surely as fat in a fire when the lover draws close.
edges.quote: hearts are like fat in a fire

couplets.gloss: My eyes have gone dull from watching for him and my fingertips are worn down from counting the days marked on the wall.

edges.reason: Gives longing its mark: eyes gone dull and fingers worn from counting the days.
edges.quote: my fingers have worn down

edges.reason: The wait has cost her eyes their shine.
edges.quote: My eyes have lost their lustre

couplets.gloss: What if I did forget him today, my friend? My looks have already gone and my bangle has already dropped from my arm.

edges.reason: Forgetting him, she says, would only send her bangles sliding from her arms.
edges.quote: the bangles will slip from my arms

edges.reason: Put to her maid, as if answering a friend’s advice to forget him.
edges.quote: You in your bright jewels, if I forget him today

couplets.gloss: He left because he wanted victories; the only reason I'm still alive is that I want him back.

edges.reason: Sets his wanting of victory beside hers for his return, the one thing that keeps her alive.
edges.quote: Wanting his return, I am still alive.

couplets.sensitive: Ties staying alive to an absent lover.

couplets.gloss: He went off with no thought for my feelings, and yet just imagining him coming home makes my heart leap.
Just let me look at my husband until I've seen enough of him: the sickly colour will leave my thin arm for good.

edges.reason: One full sight of him, she says, and the pallor will be gone from her shoulders.
edges.quote: the pallor will leave my soft shoulders

edges.reason: All she asks is for her eyes to gorge on the sight of him.
edges.quote: let my eyes take their fill of the sight of my beloved

couplets.gloss: Just let him come home: in a single day I'll take in all of him, and everything that's been wearing me down will be gone.

edges.reason: His presence is a divine drink she plans to swallow in one day.
edges.quote: drink the nectar of his presence

edges.reason: His return is the one remedy for the illness of waiting.
edges.quote: until all this sickness of grief is gone

couplets.gloss: When my darling finally gets home, will I sulk at him, throw my arms round him, or somehow do both?
keywords: angry and happy to see him

couplets.gloss: May the king start the fight and win it today, so I can get home by evening and sit down to a meal with my wife.
keywords: wanting to finish work and get home

couplets.gloss: For someone waiting on a loved one far away and marking off the calendar, a single day drags like a whole week.

edges.reason: Gives longing its own clock, on which one day passes at the pace of seven.
edges.quote: one day passes like seven

edges.reason: Speaks of everyone who waits for someone far away, not of one speaker alone.
edges.quote: For those who pine, counting on the day

couplets.gloss: What good will it do to get back, to see her, even to hold her, if her heart has already broken by then?
You can try to hide it, love, but your eyes won't be held back: they tell me there's something on your mind.

edges.reason: Her eye acts on its own, slipping her control to tell him what she keeps back.
edges.quote: your kohl-dark eyes slip your control

edges.reason: Said straight to her, coaxing out what she will not say.
edges.quote: Though you hide it

couplets.gloss: My innocent girl, lovely to look at and slender-armed, holds herself back with more restraint than any other woman.
keywords: she keeps her feelings to herself

edges.reason: Admires her for holding back even beyond what a woman's composure usually asks.
edges.quote: More than a woman’s reserve hath my artless one

edges.reason: Praises looks that fill his whole sight, down to arms like bamboo.
edges.quote: beauty that fills my eyes and arms like bamboo

couplets.gloss: I can make out a thought in her, plain to see however she hides it, like a string running through a clear bead.

edges.reason: A concealed thought shows through her as thread shows through a bead, hidden and seen at once.
edges.quote: Like the thread that shows through a bead

couplets.gloss: Like the scent shut up in a flower that hasn't opened, her half smile is holding something back.

edges.reason: A budding smile carries a meaning without yet giving it, which is how lovers speak.
edges.quote: something lies inside the budding smile

edges.reason: The closed bud keeps its fragrance as her smile keeps her thought.
edges.quote: As fragrance lies inside a closed bud

couplets.gloss: The sly way she hid what she was feeling and walked off has something in it that cures my pain.

edges.reason: Delights in the very slyness with which she kept her thought from him.
edges.quote: The stealth of the woman in close-set bangles

edges.reason: His pain finds its medicine in the one who gave it to him.
edges.quote: holds a medicine

couplets.gloss: He's being unusually sweet to me. I'm afraid he's hiding something, and that it means he's about to leave me again.

edges.reason: His extra sweetness is the very thing that frightens her: she reads in it another leaving.
edges.quote: in it I see myself bearing pain again

couplets.gloss: My bangle sensed the chill in my husband's heart even before I did.

edges.reason: Her bangles know he has drawn away before she does.
edges.quote: My bangles knew before we did

couplets.gloss: He only left yesterday, yet I feel as if I've been fading for a week already.

edges.reason: Her body has been pale for seven days, over a man gone for one.
edges.quote: pale in body for seven days

couplets.gloss: She looked at her bangle, then at her soft arm, then down at her feet, and that was her whole message to me.

edges.reason: A whole plea is made in three glances, with not one word spoken.
edges.quote: She looked at her bangles, looked at her soft arms, looked at her feet.

edges.reason: Her look at the bangle warns what will become of it if he goes.
edges.quote: She looked at her bangles

edges.reason: The maid acts as go-between, passing her mistress’s silent signs on to him.
edges.quote: That is what she did there.

couplets.gloss: She tells me what parting would do to her and asks to come with me, all with a look: no woman could be more delicate.

edges.reason: Admires a woman who will plead the sickness of desire with her eyes but won’t say it aloud.
edges.quote: womanhood on top of womanhood

edges.reason: Her eyes alone carry a whole request, and he marvels at it.
edges.quote: To tell the sickness of desire with the eyes and beg

couplets.gloss: Getting high just from thinking of someone and happy just from seeing them: drink can't do that, only love can.

edges.reason: Claims for desire alone a joy that comes at a thought and at a glance.
edges.quote: toddy can’t do this, but desire can

edges.reason: Toddy is the rival that fails the test, since it delights only when actually drunk.
edges.quote: toddy can’t do this

couplets.gloss: When love has grown as tall as a palm tree, there can't be room for even a grain's worth of sulking.

edges.reason: A palmyra’s height of desire leaves no space for a millet seed’s worth of sulk.
edges.quote: as tall as a palmyra

couplets.gloss: Even though he ignores me and does whatever he likes, my eyes can't settle until they've seen him.
couplets.sensitive: presents needing one who neglects her as natural

edges.reason: However little he cares, her eyes go on demanding the sight of him.
edges.quote: my eyes can’t rest without seeing my husband

couplets.gloss: I set out to give him the cold shoulder, my friend, but my heart forgot all about that and ran to be with him.

edges.reason: Owns up to her friend that the plan to sulk fell apart.
edges.quote: I went there to sulk, my friend

couplets.gloss: An eye can't see the make-up stick while it's being lined; in the same way I can't see his faults when he's close.

edges.reason: The eye that cannot see the pencil touching it pictures her blindness to him up close.
edges.quote: the eye seeth not the blackness of the pencil

couplets.gloss: When he's in front of me I can't find anything wrong with him; when he's away, faults are all I can find.
Nobody leaps into a river knowing it will sweep them off; so why start a sulk I know I can't keep up once he is near?
A drunk still wants drink even though it shames him; your chest is the same to me, you deceiver, whatever you've done.
keywords: going back to someone who hurts you
couplets.sensitive: welcomes back one who hurts and shames her

edges.reason: She is the drinker who keeps going back to the toddy that disgraces her.
edges.quote: is like toddy to those drunk on it

edges.reason: Said to his face, with a name that is half reproach and half endearment.
edges.quote: you thief

couplets.gloss: Love is more delicate than any blossom, and only a few people know how to handle it gently enough.

edges.reason: Says what desire is: so soft that few ever find it at its peak.
edges.quote: Few ever find it at its peak

edges.reason: The flower sets the measure of softness, and desire goes beyond it.
edges.quote: Desire is softer than a flower.

couplets.gloss: She was glaring at me when she saw me, but when I came near she rushed to hold me even faster than I went to her.
You can see how his heart does exactly what he wants. So why, my heart, won't you stand with me?

edges.reason: Envies him a heart that obeys and demands the same loyalty from her own.
edges.quote: won’t you stand by me?

couplets.gloss: You can see he doesn't care about me, heart, and still you go to him as if he were on our side.

edges.reason: Accuses her heart of going to the man who isn’t drawn to her.
edges.quote: you go to him

couplets.gloss: You trail after him whenever you feel like it, heart. Is that because people who are down have no friends, even their own hearts?

edges.reason: Charges her heart with deserting her, as friends desert the ruined.
edges.quote: the ruined have no friends

couplets.gloss: You won't even sulk a little first, heart, before showing how happy you are with him. Who will plot anything with you after this?

edges.reason: Rebukes her heart as a useless accomplice that rushes to him without the agreed sulk.
edges.quote: You won’t sulk first and enjoy him after.

couplets.gloss: My heart is afraid of not having him, and once it has him it's afraid of losing him: the worry never stops.

edges.reason: Shows the fear outlasting success: to have him at last is only to start dreading his loss.
edges.quote: when it has him it fears parting

couplets.gloss: What use is my heart? When I sit thinking on my own, all it does is eat away at me.

edges.reason: Turns on her heart as a worthless thing whose only skill is gnawing at her.
edges.quote: only to eat me up

couplets.gloss: Stuck with this silly heart that can't forget him and keep its pride, I've lost sight of my own dignity too.

edges.reason: Blames her fall on bad company, and the company is her own heart.
edges.quote: Caught up with this worthless, foolish heart

couplets.gloss: My heart, which loves him as much as life, thinks it beneath us to run him down, so it always takes his side.
Who will stand by you in your sorrow if your own heart won't help you?
If my own heart isn't on my side, why should I be surprised that strangers don't care about me?
Don't hug him yet, dear. Pretend to be cross, and let's have a bit of fun watching him squirm.

edges.reason: The maid urges a sulk for the sport of seeing him suffer a little.
edges.quote: Sulk, and let us see

edges.reason: Playful counsel to the woman herself on how to receive him.
edges.quote: Don’t embrace him.

couplets.gloss: A little sulking gives love its flavour, but if it drags on it spoils things, the way over-seasoning ruins a meal.

edges.reason: Says what the sulk is: the seasoning of union, good only in small measure.
edges.quote: A sulk is like the right amount of salt.

edges.reason: Gives a working rule for any tiff: a little does no harm, so do not drag it out.
edges.quote: Drawing it out is like a little too much.

couplets.gloss: Leaving without holding the person you've upset is like hurting someone who is already hurt.

edges.reason: Said to the man’s face: leaving a sulking woman unembraced adds to her pain.
edges.quote: Not to embrace those who sulk with you

edges.reason: Warns against leaving a quarrel open: it hurts someone who is hurting already.
edges.quote: like bringing fresh pain to people already in distress

couplets.gloss: Refusing to make peace with someone who's sulking is like hacking at the roots of a plant that's already dying.

edges.reason: Shows what refusing to make up does: it cuts at the root of something already withering.
edges.quote: cutting a withered creeper at the root

edges.reason: Leaving someone’s sulk unsoothed cuts at the root a creeper already withered.
edges.quote: cutting a withered creeper at the root

couplets.gloss: A sulk from the woman you love has a pull even on people of perfect goodness.

edges.reason: Grants the sulk a grace that adorns even those of fine character.
edges.quote: What graces those of fine character

couplets.gloss: Without the odd quarrel and sulk, love would be like fruit that never reaches its proper ripeness.

edges.reason: Treats deep and light sulks as what desire can’t do without.
edges.quote: Without the deep sulk and the light one

edges.reason: Desire without sulking is fruit gone past its best, or fruit too green to eat.
edges.quote: a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green

couplets.gloss: Even sulking hurts in one way: you keep wondering how long it will be before you make up.

edges.reason: Finds the one true pain inside the game: not knowing how far off the making-up is.
edges.quote: There is a pain even in sulking

couplets.gloss: What's the point of suffering when there's no one who loves me around to see how much it hurts?
Water is only nice in the shade, and a sulk is only sweet coming from someone who truly loves you.

edges.reason: Sets its test: a sulk is sweet only with those who love you.
edges.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you

couplets.gloss: If my heart still wants someone who leaves me to sulk alone and won't make peace, that's nothing but silly craving.
keywords: she never makes the first move

edges.reason: Brands his own yearning for a woman who leaves a sulk to wither as mere craving.
edges.quote: That is only craving.

couplets.gloss: Every woman feasts her eyes on you, you flirt. I'm not coming anywhere near you.
keywords: jealous of how people look at him

edges.reason: Refuses his embrace because, she says, every woman’s eyes have already had their share of him.
edges.quote: eat you up with their eyes

edges.reason: Flung directly at him, with “philanderer” as the taunt.
edges.quote: you philanderer

couplets.gloss: I was sulking and he sneezed, knowing I'd be bound to say 'bless you' and so break my silence.
keywords: trick to end a silent treatment

edges.reason: His sneeze is a ruse to force a blessing from a woman refusing to speak.
edges.quote: He knew I would say, “Live long.”

couplets.gloss: Even if I put a flower in my hair she gets annoyed and says I'm dressing up for some other woman's benefit.
keywords: accused of dressing up for someone else

edges.reason: A flower is enough: her suspicion turns it into proof of another woman.
edges.quote: You wear it to show some woman

couplets.gloss: I told her I loved her more than anyone, and she frowned and demanded: more than who? more than who?

edges.reason: A vow of love is heard as an admission that there are others to compare her with.
edges.quote: Than who? Than who?

couplets.gloss: I told her we'd never part in this life, and straight away her eyes filled with tears at the thought of the next one.
I told her I'd thought of her while I was away, and she pulled back from hugging me: so you had forgotten me, then!

edges.reason: Finds a sulk in a tender remark: to have remembered her, she says, is to have forgotten her.
edges.quote: So why did you forget me?

couplets.gloss: I sneezed and she said 'bless you', then took it back and cried: who was thinking of you, to make you sneeze?

edges.reason: Her blessing turns to tears the moment she wonders who else has him in mind.
edges.quote: Who was thinking of you, that you sneezed?

edges.reason: A sneeze, the sign of being remembered, becomes evidence of a rival.
edges.quote: I sneezed and she blessed me.

couplets.gloss: So I held in a sneeze, and she cried anyway: you're hiding from me that someone of yours is thinking about you!

edges.reason: Now it is the concealing that offends, so nothing he does can clear him.
edges.quote: Are you hiding from me

edges.reason: The stifled sneeze springs the trap that the open one had set.
edges.quote: I held back a sneeze

couplets.gloss: However hard I try to calm her, she only gets angrier: you've obviously had plenty of practice on other women!

edges.reason: His very skill at soothing her is taken as proof that there have been others.
edges.quote: So this is how you are with others too.

couplets.gloss: Even when I'm simply gazing at her in admiration she snaps: whose body are you comparing mine with?

edges.reason: Even rapt admiration of her own beauty is suspected of a hidden comparison.
edges.quote: Who are you thinking of, looking at all of me like that?

couplets.gloss: Even when he's done nothing wrong, sulking is how I get to enjoy him coaxing me round.

edges.reason: She sulks at a faultless man for the tenderness it draws out of him.
edges.quote: sulking is what draws out his tenderness

couplets.gloss: His kindness may be held up for a little while, but there's real pleasure in the small sting of being cross.

edges.reason: Counts the small hurt of sulking as worth it, since his tenderness comes back greater.
edges.quote: The small hurt of sulking

couplets.gloss: Is any paradise better than a lovers' sulk, when the two of you are as blended as water and the ground it runs on?

edges.reason: Asks whether heaven itself can beat it, so long as the pair are truly one.
edges.quote: Is there any heaven better than a lovers’ quarrel

couplets.gloss: Right inside my quarrel with the one I love is the very thing that breaks down my resistance.

edges.reason: The quarrel carries its own undoing: inside it is the weapon that breaks her resolve.
edges.quote: is the weapon that breaks my resolve

couplets.gloss: Even when you've done nothing wrong, there's a certain pleasure in the one you love pulling her arms away from you.

edges.reason: Being kept from her soft shoulders is the sulk’s gesture, and even the innocent party finds pleasure in it.
edges.quote: being kept from the soft shoulders of the one you love has a pleasure of its own

couplets.gloss: A meal feels better once it has settled than while you eat it; in the same way a lovers' tiff is sweeter than their embrace.

edges.reason: Ranks the quarrel above the embrace, as a meal well settled above the eating of it.
edges.quote: a quarrel is sweeter than making love

couplets.gloss: In a lovers' quarrel the one who gives in first has really won, as you find out when you make up.
couplets.sensitive: counsel to yield first could reach someone pressured to give in

edges.reason: Settles who comes out ahead in a lovers’ quarrel: the one who loses has won.
edges.quote: the one who loses has won

couplets.gloss: Will she put on a little quarrel for a while, and so give our lovemaking some extra spice?

edges.reason: Hopes another quarrel will bring back the sweetness of their lovemaking.
edges.quote: Will a quarrel bring back the sweetness of our lovemaking

couplets.gloss: Let her go on frowning and pouting a bit longer, and let the night last as long as I ask it to.

edges.reason: He wants more of her sulking, and is in no hurry for it to end.
edges.quote: Let her go on sulking

edges.reason: Night is begged to stay, so that the sweet quarrel can run on.
edges.quote: let the night run on while I plead

couplets.gloss: Sulking is what makes love delightful, and what makes sulking delightful is the hug at the end of it.

edges.reason: The book’s last word on the sulk: it is the joy of desire.
edges.quote: Sulking is the joy of desire

edges.reason: Sets the embrace of reconciliation above even the sweetness of the quarrel.
edges.quote: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it

ideaLinks.reason: She tells her heart that desire and modesty can’t both be borne: one has to go.
ideaLinks.quote: give up desire or give up modesty

ideaLinks.reason: The flood of desire sweeps away the shame and strength he trusted, and in K1138 it breaks through her hiding too.
ideaLinks.quote: The fierce flood of desire carries off the raft

ideaLinks.reason: Desire’s axe breaks the door, and modesty’s bolt gives way with it.
ideaLinks.quote: The axe of desire breaks down the door of reserve, bolted with modesty

ideaLinks.reason: Desire leaves no room to sulk: every attempt at it collapses the moment he is near.
ideaLinks.quote: I went off meaning to sulk. I saw my heart was ready to join him

ideaLinks.reason: A sulk has its sweetness only with those who love you, as water has its sweetness in the shade.
ideaLinks.quote: sulking is sweet with those who love you

ideaLinks.reason: Without sulks deep and light, desire is fruit too ripe or too green.
ideaLinks.quote: Without the deep sulk and the light one, desire is like a fruit too ripe and a fruit too green.

ideaLinks.reason: The sulk closes in an embrace, and that embrace is its whole sweetness.
ideaLinks.quote: the joy of sulking is the embrace that ends it

proposals.label: The Plant and Its Roots
proposals.why: Kural 1304, the guide's own example of an image, cuts the roots of a starving plant, but the vocabulary covers only trees. Watered and rooted plants recur in 595, 718, 1093 and 1147.
